name: Pelagianism

attributes.attribute: a belief that all life is good
a British or Irish Christian thinker

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Pelagianism is a cosmological idea tied to the teacher Pelagius. This fifth-century Christian thinker was likely a Celt, British or Irish by birth. His rival Saint Jerome said Pelagius was stuffed with Irish porridge. Pelagius drew many followers among early Christians through his happy heresy. He held that all creation was good. The human task, he said, was to learn to love all that exists. The cleric Augustine of North Africa fought against this view. Augustine had been shaped in his youth by the dualistic thought of Mani. His struggle with Pelagianism became a turning point for the early church, because Pelagianism showed a Celtic view of nature.

okr.objective: Summarize Pelagianism and the church dispute around it.
